faq.html:
What does Spindle do?

Spindle is a GPU compute network design built on Robinhood Chain. Providers register GPU nodes and serve AI jobs in the open lane; sealed is in testing. Each job emits a signed receipt and verified earnings accrue in USDG. The payout design offers USDG, canonical Stock Tokens or a virtual card, with split claims supported. This site presents the v1.1 specification and an illustrative dashboard; it does not display live earnings or guarantee demand.

Which GPUs and APIs are supported?

The specification includes sealed-lane confidential GPUs such as H100, H200 and B200-class hardware, alongside an open lane for non-sensitive work on suitable consumer GPUs. The API design supports chat completions, embeddings and images. The node agent benchmarks each GPU and detects its available lane; production access details are coming soon.

What does a receipt prove?

Each completed job emits a COSE receipt signed by the node key. Verification checks the signature, job-to-billing match and measured units before recording USDG earnings. Hourly cumulative Merkle roots support provider claims. A receipt evidences work on the measured stack; it does not prove the AI output was correct.

Which compute lane is private?

Only the sealed lane is designed to keep prompts private from the operator. It requires eligible confidential GPUs, a TDX environment and current attestation, with OHTTP for the request path. Open-lane jobs are not confidential. The specification discloses TEE limits and does not establish a SOC 2 audit.

How do the payout routes work?

Verified earnings accrue in USDG. The claim design offers a USDG wallet transfer, a quote for a canonical Stock Token, or a virtual card through a third-party program. Split claims share the same cumulative entitlement. Card regions and terms, as well as Stock Token liquidity and issuer eligibility, determine which route is available.

How does node onboarding work?

The intended onboarding flow starts with one Docker command. The agent benchmarks the GPU, detects confidential-compute support, creates a node key and registers through a passkey smart account on Robinhood Chain. The website is a specification preview; it does not promise a setup time or provide live node enrollment.
